key_insight: The paper shows how counterfactual simulator rollouts can be used to forecast outcomes under a new decision policy before real-world data exists. It reframes prediction as a Sim2Real transfer problem: learn from simulated trajectories under the target policy, then evaluate how well those forecasts carry over to reality.
problem_solved: It addresses the cold-start problem in policy-dependent prediction, where historical data reflect old policies and there are no real observations yet for a newly deployed policy.
method: Roll out the target policy inside a simulator to generate counterfactual trajectories.
Use these simulated trajectories to train or evaluate forecasting models for policy-dependent outcomes.
Measure how predictions transfer from simulation to real-world behavior in a Sim2Real setting.
impact: This helps AI/ML practitioners anticipate the effects of a new policy without waiting for extensive live deployment data. It is especially useful for decision-making systems where actions influence future observations, such as operations, healthcare, robotics, and reinforcement learning.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pipeline diagram: historical policy data -> simulator rollouts -> real-world deployment

paper_title: Forecasting from Counterfactual Simulator Rollouts: A Sim2Real Evaluation
paper_authors: Angel Wang, Dominique Perrault-Joncas, Alvaro Maggiar, Dean Foster, Carson Eisenach
